title: Parades and early clarinet idols; Papa Tio and the Bocquets
summary: Funeral parades with Oliver, Ory and Celestin bands, clarinetists he heard, the Bocquets, and Papa Tio's son Lorenzo.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Do you remember any parades when you were a kid? The brass bands?
Oh yes, I remember the parade very well.
Do you remember which bands they were or did you follow any of those musicians? Certain ones that you liked when you were a kid that were your idols you might say and you tried to follow them more?

Well, I followed the parade true enough, yes, because it's King Oliver, he played and so did Ory. He had a band in Celestan and those are the three bands that mostly got the funeral parades to my knowledge.
Can you remember the clarinet players in there, who they were that you...
I had Big Eye Louie and Bessier. Let's see, who else?
Well, yeah, later Johnny Dodd did play a couple of funerals, I do remember that.
Do you remember George Bocquet when you were young, hearing him?
I remember Charlie Bocquet. Do you know him?
No, no, I only, I met George was the only one I ever knew.
Charlie was a trumpet player wasn't he? Charlie called it? Charlie Bocquet.

Charlie Bocquet. You had another brother who played clarinet didn't he? Iseal. Iseal Bocquet. Somebody told us about another brother too, that you once said you didn't remember him. I don't know who that was. Do you remember some of them? Little Bocquet? Mm-hmm. Talked like you had another third brother. I mean, there were three of them. But do you remember the Teos? Did you tell us something about the Papa Teo was your teacher?
Yes, he was. He was a wonderful old man.
I think it happened to go to him.

I was living near down there, San Bernard and Durjan War. He's a little bit more towards Canal Street. And I know his son, Lorenda, because he played a C clarinet. And he was the only one who had a job that if he did lay it off, that I had a chance to go and play for a dollar and a half. I did play a few jobs before I left New Orleans, but no record of those things, see.
